original_question: If a graph G has maximum degree Delta, must its L(2,1)-labeling number satisfy lambda_{2,1}(G) <= Delta^2?
target_in_paper: Section 5.2, the L(2,1)-Labeling Conjecture; restated in Section 6 as Question 14.
correct_elements: The draft already matches the paper's intended target very closely: it asks about the global Griggs-Yeh L(2,1)-Labeling Conjecture for graphs of maximum degree Δ and uses the correct proposed upper bound λ_{2,1}(G) <= Δ^2.
missing_details: The paper quantifies over every graph G; the stand-alone statement should make the universal quantifier explicit.
Δ should be identified as the maximum degree Δ(G) of G.
λ_{2,1}(G) should be defined, not just named: it is the minimum span of an L(2,1)-labeling of G.

An L(2,1)-labeling should be defined: it is an assignment of positive integers to V(G) such that adjacent vertices get labels differing by at least 2 and vertices at distance 2 get distinct labels (equivalently, labels differing by at least 1).
The span should be specified as the difference between the largest and smallest labels used.

The question should make clear that no extra hypotheses such as planarity, bounded diameter, connectedness, girth conditions, or 'Δ sufficiently large' are part of the conjecture as stated in the paper.
refined_question: Does every graph G with maximum degree Δ(G)=Δ satisfy λ_{2,1}(G) <= Δ^2, where λ_{2,1}(G) is the minimum span of an L(2,1)-labeling of G, that is, an assignment f:V(G) to the positive integers such that |f(u)-f(v)| >= 2 whenever uv is an edge of G and f(u) != f(v) whenever dist_G(u,v)=2?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 5.2 rather than an earlier numbered conjecture: the paper states in Section 5.2 that the L(2,1)-Labeling Conjecture is 'Every graph G has λ_{2,1}(G) <= Δ^2,' immediately after defining L(p,q)-labelings, span, and λ_{p,q}(G). The same statement is restated in the open-problems list as Question 14 in Section 6. Nearby context also shows the intended scope: Theorem 41 says the conjectured bound is known for sufficiently large Δ, and Theorem 42 proves it for graphs of diameter 2, so the uncluttered universal version is the exact open problem the draft is aiming at. Because this is a graph-labeling question, algebraic items such as ambient ring/field, homogeneity, or nilpotency are not applicable here.

citations.label: definition of L(p,q)-labeling, span, and λ_{p,q}(G)
